messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] SEV2 - Elevated 5xxs observed for control-plane-backed endpoints (config + org-lookup). Pager opened. Paging maya (oncall) and backend oncall. See dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/controlplane/errors
maya (oncall): saw the pager. looking at logs now. can someone confirm scope — is this auth/orglookup/config or multiple? :eyes:
ryan (backend): early signal shows a spike of 502/504s from gateway -> controlplane-config (timeout) and increased 5xxs from org-lookup fanout. rolling traces: https://traces.internal/redwood/trace/abcd1234
jun (infra): infra metrics show controlplane config service error rate jumped at 14:02 UTC, CPU okay, but request queue depth spiked. possible cache stampede or bad rollout.
carla (support): getting a couple of customer reports: 2 enterprise tenants reporting failed model requests ~ 14:05. CS triage inbound.
maya (oncall): quick customer impact check: can we get 5m error rate and approximate affected users?
ryan (backend): pulling from logs: ```
ERROR upstream_response: code=502 target=config-service path=/v1/config/resolve latency_ms=12034
WARN orglookup fanout error: timeout after 10s for tenant=acme-co
```
ryan (backend): counts: approx 11.8% 5xx for text-generate route last 10m, config-service originating ~65% of those. org-lookup contributed ~25%.
olivia (product): any recent config or feature flags rolled today on control plane? I pushed a small rollout at 13:50 (config cache TTL change) but it was low risk.
ryan (backend): that TTL change could be it if it caused cache to expire and trigger mass rebuilds. checking rollout: flagged candidates show a canary started at 13:48.
deploy-bot: deploy event: config-service v2.3.1 rollout started by olivia at 2025-06-12T13:48:03Z. Pod restarts: 0. healthchecks mostly passing until 14:01Z.
jun (infra): hypothesis: new TTL + warmup path caused simultaneous heavy backend calls -> queue saturation -> timeouts -> gateway 502s.
maya (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout / revert TTL change 2) enable degraded cached mode in gateway to serve last-known config 3) increase circuit-breaker timeouts to prevent upstream cascade 4) scale config-service replicas 5) alert CS with ETA
ryan (backend): executing revert of TTL flag now (feature-flag service): `ffctl set config.cache_ttl_backfill off --actor ryan --note "hotfix revert"`
ryan (backend): revert acknowledged. patch applied to flags.
jun (infra): scaling config-service from 4 -> 8 replicas and increasing request queue worker pool. `kubectl scale deploy/config-service --replicas=8 -n controlplane`
jun (infra): scaling in progress, new pods joining.
maya (oncall): enabling degraded cached mode on gateway: `gatewayctl set-mode degraded-config-cache` — this will let gateway serve cached responses up to TTL instead of calling controlplane for every request. Doing it now.
maya (oncall): also bumped circuit-breaker threshold and timeout to 15s to reduce cascades: `svc-config set circuit.timeout 15000`
deploy-bot: rollback triggered: config-service rollback to v2.3.0 by ryan at 14:12:09Z. rollout status: progressing...
ryan (backend): verifying traces after rollback... initial signs: error rate dropping from 11.8% -> 6.1% within 3m.
carla (support): CS update: informed affected customers of degradation and that we're working on a mitigation. two customers asked for ETA, provided ~30m.
olivia (product): noting this as a config-release-induced incident. need follow-up RCA and tighten rollout circuit-breakers in release flow.
maya (oncall): ok error rate now at ~2.4% last 5m, gateway 502s down to baseline-ish. keeping degraded config-cache mode on for 30m while we stabilize.
jun (infra): we still saw a few slow requests with 504 due to long-running backfills; I'm increasing backoff for backfills to avoid throttling core path. patching now.
ryan (backend): added temporary rate limiter for org-lookup fanout: `orglookup.rate.limit=200/s` to dampen concurrent sweeps.
pagerduty: pager escalated to SRE lead (ryan) at 14:15 UTC.
maya (oncall): Incident assessment for handoff: start 14:02 UTC, major spike peaked 14:06, mitigations applied 14:12 (rollback + scale + degraded mode), significant reduction by 14:18. Impact window ~16 minutes. Affected surface: generation API upstream errors ~12% peak, ~3 enterprise customers exceeded 5% error rate. No data loss, errors are transient 5xx.
olivia (product): customer impact: logged tickets from Acme and BetaCorp; priority follow-up with account teams.
carla (support): creating post-incident customer summary to send to enterprise accounts.
maya (oncall): next steps: 1) keep degraded config-cache on for 30m 2) verify no residual backfill jobs running 3) run controlled canary for TTL change in staging with synthetic traffic 4) schedule RCA and action items: stricter rollout throttles + pre-warm cache + rollout kill-switch
ryan (backend): I'll own the rollback RCA items. will collect traces, logs, and the feature-flag rollout history.
jun (infra): I'll add automation to prevent simultaneous backfills across replicas and add autoscaling policy for controlplane queue depth.
olivia (product): schedule postmortem sync with eng, infra, and CS tomorrow.
maya (oncall): handoff note for next oncall (tom): incident stabilized, mitigations in place, followups assigned: ryan (rollback RCA), jun (autoscale+backoff), olivia (release flow changes), carla (customer comms). Leaving degraded mode on until 14:42 UTC unless objections.
carla (support): ack. prepping customer comms draft, will share in #support for review.
ryan (backend): adding one more item — add synthetic check in CI that exercises config TTL hot path to detect stampedes in canary.
maya (oncall): closing pager, setting severity to P2 post-mitigation. Thank you team. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=stabilized severity=P2 owner=maya. Link: https://incidents.internal/2812340000
maya (oncall): logging handoff and timestamped notes in the incident doc. leaving channel.
